# `proj ignore`

Choose which project paths Git or R package builds should exclude. Existing
user-written rules are preserved outside the managed block.

## `proj ignore add`

Manually appends one or more raw file or directory paths to the project ignore files.

Unlike automatic configurations driven by `_proj.yml`, these manual entries represent permanent, user-specified exclusions and are placed strictly *above* the `# --- PROJ MANAGED ---` blocks.

### Arguments & Flags

- `<PATHS>...`: One or more raw file or directory paths to be ignored.
- `--force-create`: Boolean flag (default `true`). If true, creates ignore files if they don't exist. If false, skips file creation unless the project requires it (e.g. finding a `.git` folder or a `DESCRIPTION` file).
- `--type`: Optional filter selection (`all` [default], `git`, `rbuild`). Determines which ignore file receives the manual path entries. Note that `.Rbuildignore` is skipped entirely if no `DESCRIPTION` file exists at the project root.

## `proj ignore remove`

Manually forces paths to be tracked by appending negated syntax (e.g. `!path/` or `^!pattern$`).

These unignore entries represent permanent, user-specified negations and are placed strictly *below* the `# --- END PROJ MANAGED ---` boundary in `.gitignore` and `.Rbuildignore` files.

### Arguments & Flags

- `<PATHS>...`: One or more raw file or directory paths to force tracking.
- `--type`: Optional filter selection (`all` [default], `git`, `rbuild`). Determines which ignore file receives the negated entries. Note that `.Rbuildignore` is skipped entirely if no `DESCRIPTION` file exists at the project root.

## When automatic rules are updated

Directory initialization and production builds update the managed ignore rules
from `_proj.yml`. Reading configuration (`proj yml read`) and looking up paths
leave ignore files unchanged. A preview does not add ignore rules.

The project is selected by `--project`, an inherited build context, or the nearest
recognized parent project folder. A VERSION file is one possible marker; it is
not required for every query. See [project discovery](path.qmd#nearest-root-discovery).

## Git and R package exclusions

- `.gitignore` controls which untracked files Git normally ignores.
- `.Rbuildignore` excludes files when building an R source package. It is only
  updated when the project has a DESCRIPTION file; it does not prove CRAN compliance.

These files use different pattern languages: Git uses ignore patterns, while
R uses regular expressions. projcli converts configured paths for each file.
Check manual patterns carefully, especially when keeping a file that a parent
folder rule excludes.

## Your rules are preserved

Automatic rules are kept between these comments:

```text
# --- PROJ MANAGED ---
# --- END PROJ MANAGED ---
```

projcli replaces only the content inside its managed block. Existing rules
outside it are preserved. If the block is missing, it is appended. Manual add
entries go before the block; manual remove entries go after it.
